exact_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n, let h be a smooth positive Hermitian form, and let mu be a smooth positive probability volume. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial. For a smooth background theta admitting a smooth positive representative theta+dd^c u, define
D_mu(gamma)=integral_X (mu/gamma^n)^(1/n)gamma^n,
lambda_mu(theta)=inf_gamma [integral_X theta wedge gamma^(n-1)]/D_mu(gamma),
where gamma ranges over smooth positive Hermitian metrics satisfying dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0 (in dimension one lambda is the integral). Put V_mu=lambda_mu^n.
Choose a finite-dimensional real space V of smooth real (1,1) forms with V intersect dd^c C^infinity(X,R)={0}. Let C consist of those backgrounds in V with a smooth positive representative. The smooth positive Hessian metric is g=-D^2 log lambda_mu, restricted to this specified cone or to S={theta in C:lambda_mu(theta)=1}; all distances are their intrinsic Riemannian path distances.
Question: describe the metric completion of the unit-volume hypersurface for a specified geometrically meaningful family of such finite-dimensional cones, identify all Cauchy boundary points and their current representatives, and prove estimates on the minimizing Gauduchon metrics distinguishing finite from infinite distance. Find an explicit nonclosed family beyond the already-known closed two-factor projective cone and blowup-surface example, or establish a more general classification including such a family.
Known background: homogeneity gives (C,g) isometric to R times S with metric dr^2+g_S, r=log lambda. Thus volume tending to zero or infinity forces infinite length. The cone generated by the two closed factors on CP1 times CP1 is complete in logarithmic coordinates, while a boundary with positive nef volume on the blowup of CP2 can occur at finite distance. These examples do not classify other specified cones. Merely adjoining every nef class is not a completion criterion, and enlarging the cone may shorten distances.
This is a precise sufficient-condition classification subtask from the original specified-cone research question. The selected cone must be fully specified and its positivity, absence of smooth dd^c directions and volume formula proved; its complete Cauchy geometry must be established. A proof for that family does not classify arbitrary finite-dimensional nonclosed cones. No candidate family or proof is supplied.

notes.summary: Self-contained determinant-volume theorem for invariant Hermitian cones on compact complex Lie-group quotients, with normalized invariant μ. Positivity modulo dd^c is exactly matrix positivity; all invariant metrics are balanced; λ=(H det A)^(1/n), g=(1/n)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹W), and the Dμ=1 minimizing Gauduchon metric is uniquely θA/λ. Nonabelian examples have genuinely nonclosed backgrounds. Positive-current representability is exactly matrix semipositivity.
notes.detailedSummary: Let X=Γ\G be a compact quotient of a connected complex Lie group of dimension n≥2, with global left-invariant holomorphic coframe α. Put θA=(i/(2π))ΣAjk αj∧barαk, h0=θI, H=∫h0^n, and μ=h0^n/H. For any real matrix subspace W⊂Herm(n) containing a positive-definite matrix, V={θA:A∈W} has no smooth dd^c directions, and its positive-representative cone is precisely W∩Herm+(n). Compactness forces all invariant vector fields to have zero divergence; this proves balancedness of every θA and vanishing of the average matrix of dd^c u. Pointwise arithmetic-geometric mean then gives the exact λ and volume formulas without a Monge–Ampère existence theorem. Equality and an integration-by-parts energy argument establish uniqueness of the normalized minimizing Gauduchon metric. The same averaging argument applies to distributional potentials: θA+dd^c u≥0 is possible exactly when A≥0; θA itself is a smooth semipositive representative. If the Lie algebra is nonabelian, no positive θA is d-closed, and adding dd^c cannot make it closed. These conclusions require the specified invariant μ, not arbitrary μ.
notes.text:
SETUP AND THEOREM.
Let G be a connected complex Lie group of complex dimension n≥2 and Γ a discrete subgroup acting by left translations, such that X=Γ\G is compact. Fix a left-invariant holomorphic coframe α1,…,αn, which descends to X. For a Hermitian matrix A define
  θA=(i/(2π))Σj,k Ajk αj∧barαk.
The harmless choice of transpose in the coefficient convention does not change positivity, determinant, or any trace formula below. Let h0=θI, H=∫X h0^n, and μ=h0^n/H. Thus μ is a smooth positive probability volume. Let W be a real linear subspace of Herm(n) containing at least one positive-definite matrix, and set V={θA:A∈W}.
Then:
(a) V∩dd^c C∞(X,R)={0}; the specified cone of backgrounds admitting a smooth positive representative is C={θA:A∈W,A>0}.
(b) Every positive θA is balanced, hence Gauduchon.
(c) With the question's dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂, its exact variational volume is
  λμ(θA)=(H det A)^(1/n),  Vμ(θA)=H det A.
(d) The unique minimizing Gauduchon metric normalized by Dμ(γ)=1 is γA=θA/λμ(θA).
(e) The Hessian metric is exactly
  gA(U,Z)=(1/n)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z),  U,Z∈W.
(f) A background θA has a positive-current representative θA+dd^c u with u a real distribution if and only if A≥0. For such A the invariant θA is itself a smooth semipositive representative. The zero background has no nonzero positive-current representative. If the Lie algebra of G is nonabelian, every positive θA is genuinely nonclosed, and has no d-closed representative obtained by adding dd^c.

1. DIVERGENCE AND BALANCEDNESS, PROVED FROM COMPACTNESS.
Let Zj be the dual invariant holomorphic frame. Write Ω=α1∧⋯∧αn. A positive constant multiple of Ω∧barΩ is h0^n. For any invariant holomorphic vector field Z, the Lie derivative of Ω is
  LZ Ω=−tr(ad Z)Ω.
This follows by evaluating the derivative on an invariant frame and summing the diagonal entries of the bracket action. Also LZ barΩ=0: contraction with barΩ is zero, and d barΩ=0. Hence the divergence of Z with respect to h0^n is the constant −tr(ad Z). Cartan's identity and Stokes on the compact X give
  0=∫X LZ(h0^n)=−tr(ad Z)H.
Consequently tr(ad Z)=0 and ∫X Zf μ=0 for every smooth complex-valued f. Conjugate vector fields have the same zero-divergence property.
Since dΩ=0, Cartan's identity now yields d(ιZ Ω)=0. The invariant (n−1,0) forms obtained by omitting one αj form a basis and are all closed. Their conjugates are closed as well. Every θA^(n−1) is a constant linear combination of wedges of these forms and their conjugates. Therefore
  d θA^(n−1)=0.
This proves balancedness, and in particular dd^c θA^(n−1)=0. No classification theorem for complex parallelizable manifolds is being used: the compact quotients above are the explicitly selected family.

2. THE SPECIFIED CONE AND THE ABSENCE OF dd^c DIRECTIONS.
On a complex Lie group [Zj,barZk]=0, and dαj has type (2,0). Therefore the coefficient matrix of dd^c u in the above coframe is (Zj barZk u)j,k. Each coefficient has integral zero against μ, because ∫Zj f μ=0. Thus the mean coefficient matrix of θA+dd^c u is A.
If this form is smoothly positive, then for each nonzero constant vector v, its coefficient quadratic form on v is everywhere strictly positive. Its integral is the corresponding quadratic form of A, so A>0. Conversely A>0 makes θA itself positive. If θA=dd^c u, taking mean coefficients gives A=0, so θA=0. This proves both the cone description and V∩dd^c C∞={0}.
For currents the same argument is distributional: the formal adjoints of Zj and barZk annihilate constants, so the average matrix of dd^c u is still zero. The coefficient matrix of a positive (1,1) current is a positive matrix of measures in the global frame. Its mean is therefore semipositive. Necessity of A≥0 follows, and sufficiency is provided by θA itself. If A=0, the trace measure of a positive representative has zero total mass and hence vanishes. Positivity and polarization then force the entire current to vanish.
As W contains a positive A+, its ordinary coefficient closure is precisely W∩{A≥0}: each such A is approached by A+εA+. Thus this current-representability cone is also the coefficient closure, but it will not be the metric completion of the unit-volume slice.

3. EXACT VARIATIONAL FORMULA AND THE MINIMIZERS.
The determinant identity gives θA^n=(det A)h0^n=Qμ, where Q=H det A. For any smooth positive Hermitian γ, pointwise arithmetic-geometric mean gives
  (θA∧γ^(n−1))/γ^n=(1/n)trγ θA ≥ (θA^n/γ^n)^(1/n).
Integrating yields
  ∫θA∧γ^(n−1) ≥ Q^(1/n) ∫(μ/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n
                         =Q^(1/n)Dμ(γ).
This applies, in particular, to every competitor in the question. The balanced metric γ=θA is an admissible competitor and satisfies
  Dμ(θA)=Q^((n−1)/n),
so its quotient is Q^(1/n). Therefore λμ(θA)=Q^(1/n), exactly.
If a Gauduchon γ attains the infimum, the continuous nonnegative arithmetic-geometric-mean deficit has zero integral. Pointwise equality implies γ=fθA for a smooth positive f. Put q=f^(n−1). Since θA^(n−1) is closed, the Gauduchon equation becomes
  dd^c q∧θA^(n−1)=0.
For d^c=(i/(4π))(bar∂−∂), multiplication by q and integration by parts give
  0=∫q dd^c q∧θA^(n−1)=−∫dq∧d^c q∧θA^(n−1).
The last integrand is nonnegative and vanishes only where dq=0. Thus q, and hence f, is constant on connected X. Finally Dμ(cθA)=c^(n−1)λμ(θA)^(n−1). Therefore Dμ=1 singles out exactly γA=θA/λμ(θA). In particular, on λμ=1 the unique normalized minimizer is θA itself. This is an explicit solution of the minimizing-metric problem, not a formal Hessian computation.

4. THE HESSIAN FORMULA AND GENUINE NONCLOSEDNESS.
The proved formula is log λμ=(log H+log det A)/n. Differentiating det(A+tU) using det(I+tA⁻¹U) gives D log det[U]=tr(A⁻¹U). Differentiating A⁻¹ gives D(A⁻¹)[Z]=−A⁻¹ZA⁻¹. Consequently
  −D²log λμ[U,Z]=(1/n)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z).
It is real, symmetric, and strictly positive for U≠0, since for U=Z it is (1/n) times the squared Frobenius norm of the Hermitian matrix A⁻¹/²UA⁻¹/². Restriction to W remains positive.
Finally ∂θA=(i/(2π))Σj,k Ajk dαj∧barαk. If A is invertible and this vanishes, independence of the barαk and invertibility of A imply dαj=0 for every j. This says the Lie algebra is abelian. Therefore on a nonabelian example every positive θA is nonclosed. Since d(dd^c u)=0, adding a smooth dd^c potential cannot change this fact.

LIMITATIONS.
The invariant probability μ is part of the sufficient hypotheses. There is no claim here for arbitrary μ on these quotients or for arbitrary finite-dimensional cones on arbitrary compact complex manifolds. No Monge–Ampère existence theorem has been imported.

reconstruction.statement:
Let G be a connected complex Lie group of complex dimension n≥2, let Γ be a discrete subgroup acting by left translations, and suppose X=Γ\G is compact. Fix a descended left-invariant holomorphic coframe α1,…,αn. For A∈Herm(n), define θA=(i/(2π))Σj,k Ajk αj∧barαk, and put h0=θI, H=∫X h0^n, and μ=h0^n/H. Use dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂. For a smooth positive Hermitian metric γ, set Dμ(γ)=∫X(μ/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n. For a background θ admitting a smooth positive representative, set λμ(θ)=infγ (∫X θ∧γ^(n−1))/Dμ(γ), where the infimum is over smooth positive γ satisfying dd^c γ^(n−1)=0, and set Vμ(θ)=λμ(θ)^n.

Let W⊂Herm(n) be any real linear subspace containing a positive-definite matrix, let V={θA:A∈W}, and let C be the set of backgrounds in V admitting a smooth positive representative θA+dd^c u with u∈C∞(X,R). Then the following assertions hold.

1. V∩dd^c C∞(X,R)={0}, and C={θA:A∈W, A>0}. Its closure in coefficient topology is {θA:A∈W, A≥0}.

2. If Z1,…,Zn is the dual invariant holomorphic frame, every invariant holomorphic vector field Z satisfies tr(ad Z)=0 and has zero divergence with respect to h0^n. For every smooth complex-valued f, ∫X Zf μ=0; the conjugate invariant vector fields have the same property. The coefficient matrix of dd^c u in the chosen coframe is (Zj barZk u)j,k and has μ-average zero. The μ-average coefficient matrix of θA+dd^c u is A, also for real distributional u.

3. For every A∈Herm(n), dθA^(n−1)=0. In particular, every positive θA is balanced and is a Gauduchon metric. Moreover θA^n=(det A)h0^n. For A>0, writing Q=H det A, one has θA^n=Qμ, and for every smooth positive Hermitian γ, without requiring γ to be Gauduchon,
   (θA∧γ^(n−1))/γ^n=(1/n)trγ θA ≥ (θA^n/γ^n)^(1/n),
   ∫X θA∧γ^(n−1) ≥ Q^(1/n)Dμ(γ).
   Pointwise equality in this arithmetic-geometric-mean inequality holds exactly when γ is a positive scalar multiple of θA at that point.

4. For every A>0,
   λμ(θA)=(H det A)^(1/n),   Vμ(θA)=H det A.
   The Gauduchon metrics attaining the defining infimum are exactly γ=cθA with constant c>0. In particular,
   Dμ(θA)=Q^((n−1)/n),
   Dμ(cθA)=c^(n−1)λμ(θA)^(n−1),
   and the unique minimizer satisfying Dμ(γ)=1 is γA=θA/λμ(θA). On S={θA∈C:λμ(θA)=1}, this normalized minimizer is θA itself.

5. Identifying C with {A∈W:A>0},
   log λμ(θA)=(log H+log det A)/n,
   D log λμ(θA)[U]=(1/n)tr(A⁻¹U),
   gA(U,Z)=−D²log λμ(θA)[U,Z]=(1/n)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z),   U,Z∈W.
   This is a smooth real symmetric positive-definite metric: gA(U,U)=(1/n)||A⁻¹/²UA⁻¹/²||F²>0 for U≠0. The metric on S is its restriction.

6. For every A∈Herm(n), there exists a real distribution u with θA+dd^c u a positive (1,1) current if and only if A≥0. For every such A, θA itself is a smooth semipositive current representative. The zero background has no nonzero positive-current representative. Thus within V the positive-current-representable coefficient cone is exactly its coefficient closure {θA:A∈W,A≥0}.

7. If the Lie algebra of G is nonabelian, every θA with A>0 is nonclosed, and adding dd^c u cannot produce a d-closed representative.

These assertions concern the specified compact quotients, invariant coefficient spaces, and probability volume μ=h0^n/H; they make no assertion for arbitrary probability volumes or arbitrary finite-dimensional cones on other manifolds.
reconstruction.proof:
Write ν=h0^n and Ω=α1∧⋯∧αn. The invariant coframe identifies invariant real (1,1) forms injectively with Herm(n). All integrations below are on the given compact quotient X.

1. Unimodularity, integration, and coefficient averaging. The invariant holomorphic fields have holomorphic coefficients in holomorphic coordinates, so [Zj,bar Zk]=0. The structure coefficients of brackets among the Zj are constant. For an invariant holomorphic field Z, evaluation on the invariant frame gives
L_Z Ω=−tr(ad Z)Ω,   L_Z bar Ω=0.
The volume ν is a nonzero constant multiple of Ω∧bar Ω. Consequently L_Zν=−tr(ad Z)ν. Cartan's formula and Stokes' theorem give ∫X L_Zν=∫X d(i_Zν)=0. Since ∫Xν=H>0, tr(ad Z)=0. Thus L_Zν=0; conjugation proves L_bar Zν=0 as well. Applying the same argument to fν gives ∫X Zf μ=0, and likewise for conjugate invariant fields. These identities hold for complex-valued smooth f by linearity.

Because ∂bar αk=0, direct differentiation gives
∂bar∂u=Σj,k (Zj bar Zk u) αj∧bar αk.
For real u the coefficient matrix is Hermitian, using [Zj,bar Zk]=0. Each coefficient has zero μ-average by the integration identity. Hence the μ-average coefficient matrix of θA+dd^c u is A.

This also holds for distributions. Identify scalar distributions with their action on test densities φμ. Relative to μ, the formal transpose of Zj is −Zj and that of bar Zk is −bar Zk. The same differential-operator expression for the coefficients therefore extends to distributions, and
⟨Zj bar Zk u,1⟩μ=⟨u,bar Zk Zj1⟩μ=0.
Thus distributional coefficient averaging has exactly the asserted meaning and value.

2. Balanced invariant forms. The holomorphic top form Ω is d-closed: it is holomorphic and has top holomorphic degree. By the preceding calculation,
d(i_ZΩ)=L_ZΩ−i_ZdΩ=0.
The forms i_ZjΩ span all invariant (n−1,0) forms. Hence every invariant (n−1,0) form is closed, as is its conjugate. Expanding θA^(n−1) expresses it as a constant linear combination of wedges of these closed (n−1,0) and (0,n−1) forms. Therefore dθA^(n−1)=0 for every Hermitian A, including indefinite A. When A>0 this proves that θA is balanced and, in particular, Gauduchon.

Expansion of the top wedge in the coframe gives θA^n=(det A)h0^n. This determinant identity is an algebraic identity for every A.

3. Positivity cone and absence of dd^c directions. If θA+dd^c u is smoothly positive, its coefficient matrix is positive definite at every point. Its average A is then positive definite: for every fixed nonzero vector v, the average of the positive scalar v*B(x)v is positive. Conversely, if A>0, θA itself is positive. Thus the prescribed cone is precisely W∩Herm⁺(n). If θA=dd^c u, averaging gives A=0 and hence θA=0. This proves V∩dd^c C∞(X,R)={0}.

A coefficient limit of positive matrices is semipositive. Conversely, choose a fixed B∈W with B>0. Every A∈W with A≥0 is the coefficient limit of A+εB>0, ε↓0. Therefore the coefficient closure is exactly W∩{A≥0}.

4. Variational formula and all minimizers. Let A>0 and Q=H det A. Then θA^n=Qμ. At a point, write B for the positive coefficient matrix of any smooth positive γ. The wedge identity and the arithmetic-geometric-mean inequality applied to the positive eigenvalues of B^(−1/2)AB^(−1/2) give
(θA∧γ^(n−1))/γ^n=(1/n)tr(B^(−1)A) ≥ (det A/det B)^(1/n)=(θA^n/γ^n)^(1/n).
Equality holds precisely when B is a positive scalar multiple of A. Multiplying by γ^n and integrating yields
∫X θA∧γ^(n−1) ≥ Q^(1/n)∫X(μ/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n=Q^(1/n)Dμ(γ).
No Gauduchon hypothesis was used in this inequality.

The admissible metric θA attains equality, so λμ(θA)=Q^(1/n) and Vμ(θA)=H det A. If an admissible γ attains the infimum, its pointwise nonnegative AM–GM defect has integral zero and hence vanishes everywhere. Thus γ=fθA for a positive smooth function f.

It remains to impose the Gauduchon condition, rather than merely pointwise equality. Put β=θA^(n−1) and v=f^(n−1). Since dβ=0,
0=dd^c(γ^(n−1))=dd^c v∧β.
Multiplying by v, integrating, and using Stokes gives
0=∫X v dd^c v∧β=−(i/(2π))∫X ∂v∧bar∂v∧β.
The integrand on the right without its minus sign is nonnegative and is zero exactly where ∂v=0, since θA is positive. Thus dv=0. Connectedness of X and n≥2 imply that f is constant. Conversely every constant multiple cθA is balanced and attains equality. These are exactly the minimizing Gauduchon metrics.

Directly from θA^n=Qμ,
Dμ(θA)=Q^((n−1)/n),   Dμ(cθA)=c^(n−1)Q^((n−1)/n)=c^(n−1)λμ(θA)^(n−1).
Since n−1>0, Dμ(cθA)=1 has the unique solution c=1/λμ(θA). Thus γA=θA/λμ(θA), and on λμ=1 it equals θA.

5. Hessian. The exact formula just proved yields
log λμ(θA)=(log H+log det A)/n.
Differentiating the determinant, and then using D(A^(−1))[Z]=−A^(−1)ZA^(−1), gives
D log λμ[U]=(1/n)tr(A^(−1)U),
−D²log λμ[U,Z]=(1/n)tr(A^(−1)UA^(−1)Z).
For Hermitian U,Z the latter is real and symmetric by conjugation and cyclicity of trace. For U≠0,
gA(U,U)=(1/n)tr((A^(−1/2)UA^(−1/2))²)=(1/n)‖A^(−1/2)UA^(−1/2)‖F²>0.
This proves smooth positive definiteness on the specified coefficient cone, and its restriction is the stated metric on S.

6. Distributional positive representatives. Let T=θA+dd^c u be a positive (1,1) current. In the global coframe its coefficient matrix is a Hermitian matrix of distributions. Positivity means, in particular, that contraction against any constant vector v gives a positive scalar distribution: its value on every nonnegative smooth test function is nonnegative. By coefficient averaging its value on 1 is v*Av. Therefore A≥0. This argument is legitimate globally because the dual frame supplies smooth positive complementary-degree test forms for these contractions; a harmless fixed positive normalization converts their wedge pairing into scalar coefficient pairing with μ.

Conversely A≥0 makes θA a smooth semipositive (and therefore positive) current, with u=0. This proves the claimed equivalence for every A∈Herm(n), and consequently also in W.

If A=0 and T is positive, each scalar contraction Tv has Tv(1)=0. For any real smooth φ, positivity applied to ‖φ‖∞±φ gives |Tv(φ)|≤‖φ‖∞Tv(1)=0. Thus every contraction vanishes. Polarization shows that every coefficient of T vanishes, so T=0. The zero background consequently has only the zero positive-current representative.

7. Genuine nonclosedness. For invariant fields of the indicated types, the exterior derivative formula and [Zj,bar Zk]=0 give
dθA(Zj,Zk,bar Zℓ)=−θA([Zj,Zk],bar Zℓ).
If A>0 and dθA=0, nondegeneracy of its pairing between the holomorphic and antiholomorphic frames forces [Zj,Zk]=0 for all j,k. The complex Lie algebra would be abelian. Thus a nonabelian Lie algebra makes every positive invariant θA nonclosed. Finally d(dd^c u)=0, so addition of any smooth dd^c u cannot alter dθA or produce a closed representative.

All arguments used the specified invariant probability measure μ=ν/H and the prescribed invariant coefficient space. No conclusion about another probability volume or an arbitrary nonclosed cone is being inferred.

notes.summary: Complete intrinsic Cauchy geometry for every fixed linear slice of the invariant determinant cones of n1. The unit-volume hypersurface is complete and proper; there are no Cauchy boundary points. Proves the full-matrix distance formula from elementary spectral variation, lower bounds for any fixed subcone, an upper bound along a normalized chord inside that subcone, and pointwise Loewner bounds for normalized minimizing Gauduchon metrics. Nonzero semipositive coefficient boundaries have current representatives but lie at infinite distance after unit-volume normalization.
notes.detailedSummary: For W⊂Herm(n) containing a positive matrix, fix H>0, S_W={A∈W:A>0,H det A=1}, and g_A(U,Z)=tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z)/n. The full matrix cone has distance ||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||_F/√n, proved directly using eigenvalue variation; when A,B have the same determinant its explicit exponential curve stays in the same determinant slice. For general W this is only a lower bound: no enlargement of the specified cone is used for upper bounds. The normalized straight chord stays in W and S_W and gives d_W(A,B)≤||A−B||_F/(√n min(λmin A,λmin B)). In particular e^(−√n d)A≤B≤e^(√n d)A. These inequalities prove that intrinsic Cauchy sequences are precisely coefficient-convergent sequences with positive-definite limit in S_W, and prove compactness of closed bounded balls without Hopf–Rinow or any imported metric-completeness theorem. On the geometric family of n1 they are pointwise estimates on the unique Dμ=1 minimizing metrics. Any eigenvalue degeneration or explosion on S_W is infinitely distant. If A_j→A_0≠0 is semipositive singular, normalizing A_j by λ(A_j) forces this divergence, quantitatively d≥|log det A_j|/(n√n)+O(1). Zero is exceptional only as an unnormalized radial endpoint: its normalization may stay interior, but zero is not a unit-volume completion point.
notes.text:
FIXED-CONE METRIC THEOREM.
Take the family and exact metric proved in n1. In matrix notation let W⊂Herm(n) contain a positive matrix, fix H>0, and write
  C_W={A∈W:A>0},
  λ(A)=(H det A)^(1/n),
  S_W={A∈C_W:λ(A)=1}.
The metric is gA(U,Z)=tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z)/n, restricted to the indicated manifold. All distances below are intrinsic path distances. The theorem is that S_W is complete and proper, and its completion adds no points. This holds for every such W, not merely the full matrix space. The proof also supplies explicit estimates on the minimizing metrics in n1.

1. ELEMENTARY FULL-MATRIX DISTANCE FORMULA.
For the full cone Herm+(n),
  d_full(A,B)=(1/√n)||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||F.                 (1)
Here log denotes the Hermitian matrix logarithm and ||·||F the Frobenius norm. Congruence by a fixed invertible matrix is an isometry, by the trace formula for g. It is enough to prove (1) with A=I and B=C>0.
The path exp(t log C) has constant speed ||log C||F/√n and gives the upper bound.
For completeness, here is a direct lower-bound argument, so no symmetric-space distance theorem is being imported. Along a piecewise C¹ positive matrix path M(t), the ordered eigenvalues σi(t) are Lipschitz on each smooth piece and stay uniformly positive. Lipschitz continuity follows from −εI≤M(t)−M(s)≤εI and the elementary ordered-eigenvalue variational principle, with ε=||M(t)−M(s)||op. Thus fi=log σi are absolutely continuous. At almost every t,
  Σi (fi'(t))² ≤ tr((M⁻¹/²M'M⁻¹/²)²).                 (2)
To check (2), diagonalize M(t). Within an eigenspace of eigenvalue σ, the first-order eigenvalue variations are the eigenvalues of the compression of M'(t) to that eigenspace. This perturbation rule can be seen directly: conjugate M(t+s) by exp(sK), with K skew-Hermitian chosen to eliminate the off-block first-order terms between distinct eigenvalues. The resulting matrix is M(t)+s times its block-diagonal compression of M'(t)+o(s); the ordered-eigenvalue bound just used controls the o(s) eigenvalue errors. Diagonalize each compression. Its contribution to the squared norm on the right of (2) is exactly the sum of (σi'/σi)² in that block; the remaining off-block entries contribute nonnegative squares. This proves (2), including repeated eigenvalues at the almost-everywhere differentiability points.
For a path from I to C, Minkowski's inequality in Euclidean R^n now gives
  length ≥ (1/√n)∫||f'||2 ≥ (1/√n)||f(1)−f(0)||2
         = (1/√n)||log C||F.
This proves (1).
If det A=det B, the attaining curve
  M(t)=A¹/²(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)^tA¹/²                         (3)
has constant determinant. Therefore (1) is also the intrinsic distance on a full constant-determinant hypersurface. No assertion is made that (3) belongs to an arbitrary proper subspace W.

2. ESTIMATES INSIDE THE SPECIFIED SUBSPACE W.
For A,B∈S_W every W-path is also a full-matrix path. Hence
  d_W(A,B) ≥ (1/√n)||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||F.              (4)
This use of an ambient lower bound cannot shorten the intrinsic distance under discussion. For an upper bound we construct a path in the specified W. Put U=B−A,
  C(t)=A+tU,
  N(t)=C(t)/λ(C(t)).
Positive matrices form a convex cone, W is linear, and homogeneity of λ implies N(t)∈S_W. Its endpoints are A and B. Set K=C⁻¹/²UC⁻¹/². Direct differentiation, using d log λ(C)/dt=tr(C⁻¹U)/n, gives
  gN(N',N')=(1/n)tr(K²)−(1/n²)(tr K)²
            ≤ ||U||F²/(n m²),
where m=min{λmin(A),λmin(B)}>0. Indeed C(t)≥mI throughout. Consequently
  d_W(A,B) ≤ ||A−B||F/(√n min{λmin(A),λmin(B)}).        (5)
This is a wholly intrinsic upper bound along the normalized chord, not along a curve in an enlarged cone.
From (4), with d=d_W(A,B), each relative eigenvalue lies in [e^(−√n d),e^(√n d)]. Equivalently,
  e^(−√n d)A ≤ B ≤ e^(√n d)A.                         (6)
The same conclusion follows along a finite-length path with its length replacing d.

3. COMPLETE CAUCHY CLASSIFICATION AND PROPERNESS.
Let (Aj) be intrinsic Cauchy in S_W. Relative to one fixed tail element, (6) gives uniform scalar bounds mI≤Aj≤MI for all sufficiently large j. For two tail elements, (6) also implies
  ||Aj−Ak||op ≤ M(e^(√n d_W(Aj,Ak))−1).
Thus Aj is a Cauchy sequence of matrix coefficients. Its limit A lies in W because W is a closed finite-dimensional linear space; A≥mI; and continuity of determinant gives H det A=1. Hence A∈S_W. Estimate (5) then gives d_W(Aj,A)→0.
Conversely, if Aj converges in coefficients to A∈S_W, estimate (5) gives intrinsic convergence. Thus the complete, exact Cauchy criterion is:
  a sequence is Cauchy if and only if its coefficient matrices converge to a positive-definite matrix in S_W.
No eigenvalue-zero, unbounded-matrix, or other point at infinity is a Cauchy boundary point.
The same inequalities show properness. A bounded distance ball about A* is contained in the matrix order interval e^(−√n R)A*≤A≤e^(√n R)A*. The coefficient and intrinsic topologies agree by (4)–(5), so a closed distance ball is a closed subset of a compact matrix order interval with fixed determinant and W-membership. It is compact. This is a direct proof, not an application of Hopf–Rinow or an imported metric-completion statement.
In particular, if λmin(Aj)→0 or λmax(Aj)→∞ on S_W, then d_W(A*,Aj)→∞. More generally an escape from every coefficient-compact subset forces distance to infinity. Distances to a fixed reference are bounded exactly when the relative eigenvalues are uniformly bounded above and away from zero; sufficiency also follows from (5).

4. MINIMIZING-GAUDUCHON ESTIMATES AND CURRENT BOUNDARIES.
By n1, on S_W the unique Dμ=1 minimizing metric is γA=θA. The matrix order estimate (6) is therefore the pointwise tensor estimate, at every x∈X,
  e^(−√n d_W(A,B))γA ≤ γB ≤ e^(√n d_W(A,B))γA.        (7)
Finite path length forces the normalized minimizing metrics to remain uniformly positive and uniformly bounded. A Cauchy sequence of these metrics converges in C∞, because they have constant coefficients in a fixed smooth coframe. Its limit is exactly the smooth positive minimizer belonging to its limit A∈S_W.
Thus every point of the completion has the canonical smooth current representative θA; there are no additional Cauchy-boundary currents. Arbitrary potentials giving other representatives are not coordinates of the specified cone and are not new completion points.
One can also rigorously compare with the positive-current coefficient boundary. By n1, its points are precisely A≥0 in W and have canonical smooth semipositive current representatives θA. For A_j∈C_W converging to a nonzero singular A0≥0, λ(A_j)→0 and the normalized minimizing matrices
  Âj=A_j/λ(A_j)∈S_W
have λmax(Âj)→∞. Hence their intrinsic distance tends to infinity. Quantitatively, for fixed A*∈S_W, generalized eigenvalue comparison and (4) give, for all sufficiently large j,
  d_W(A*,Âj) ≥ (1/√n)log(λmax(A_j)/(λ(A_j)λmax(A*)))
              = |log det A_j|/(n√n)+O(1).             (8)
Here the O(1) is bounded because A_j→A0≠0. Thus a nonzero semipositive current representative at the coefficient boundary is explicitly excluded from the unit-volume completion by blowup of the minimizing Gauduchon metric, not merely by nomenclature such as 'nef'.
At the zero matrix, normalization may remain interior, for example A_j=t_jA* with t_j→0. This is radial collapse, not a new unit-volume point: its normalized limit is the already-existing A*. There is no zero-current point of S_W. The unnormalized cone itself has infinite distance to every determinant-zero boundary. Indeed
  |d log λ(A(t))/dt|=|(1/n)tr(A⁻¹A')|≤sqrt(gA(A',A')),
so distance dominates the absolute change of log λ. This also proves infinite distance for volume tending to infinity.

SCOPE.
This is a complete intrinsic classification for the fixed linear invariant cones under n1's sufficient hypotheses. Upper bounds and completeness use curves staying in W throughout. It does not classify arbitrary nonclosed cones, arbitrary μ, or finite-distance nef boundaries arising in other geometries.

reconstruction.statement:
Let n≥2, let W⊂Herm(n) be a real linear subspace containing a positive-definite matrix, and let H>0. Define C_W={A∈W:A>0}, λ(A)=(H det A)^(1/n), and S_W={A∈C_W:λ(A)=1}. Equip C_W with gA(U,Z)=(1/n)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z), U,Z∈W, and equip S_W with the restricted metric. Let d_W denote intrinsic Riemannian path distance on S_W, and let d_C_W denote intrinsic path distance on C_W. All the following distances are intrinsic on the specified spaces.

1. On the full cone Herm⁺(n), with the same trace metric,
   d_full(A,B)=(1/√n)||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||F.
   Congruence A↦PAP* by a fixed invertible complex matrix P is an isometry. The curve
   M(t)=A¹/²(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)^tA¹/²,   0≤t≤1,
   attains d_full(A,B). If det A=det B, M(t) has that determinant for every t; consequently the displayed distance formula is also the intrinsic distance on every full constant-determinant hypersurface.

2. For every A,B∈S_W,
   (1/√n)||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||F ≤ d_W(A,B)
   ≤ ||A−B||F/(√n min{λmin(A),λmin(B)}).
   In particular, with d=d_W(A,B),
   e^(−√n d)A ≤ B ≤ e^(√n d)A.
   For any finite-length piecewise C¹ path in S_W joining A to B, the same order inequalities hold with its length in place of d.

   More explicitly, let U=B−A, C(t)=A+tU, N(t)=C(t)/λ(C(t)), and m=min{λmin(A),λmin(B)}. Then N is a path in S_W from A to B. If K(t)=C(t)⁻¹/²UC(t)⁻¹/², then
   gN(t)(N′(t),N′(t))=(1/n)tr(K(t)²)−(1/n²)(tr K(t))²
   ≤ ||U||F²/(n m²),
   and length(N)≤||A−B||F/(√n m).

3. S_W is complete and proper: its metric completion is S_W itself, and every closed bounded intrinsic ball is compact. A sequence (Aj)⊂S_W is intrinsic Cauchy if and only if its coefficient matrices converge to a positive-definite matrix A∈W with H det A=1. In that case d_W(Aj,A)→0. Conversely, coefficient convergence to any A∈S_W implies intrinsic convergence. The coefficient and intrinsic topologies on S_W agree.

   There are no Cauchy boundary points with a zero eigenvalue, with unbounded coefficients, or at any other point at infinity. For a fixed A*∈S_W, a sequence has bounded d_W-distance from A* if and only if all eigenvalues of A*⁻¹/²AjA*⁻¹/² are uniformly bounded above and uniformly bounded away from zero. If λmin(Aj)→0 or λmax(Aj)→∞, then d_W(A*,Aj)→∞. More generally, escape from every coefficient-compact subset of S_W forces distance from A* to tend to infinity.

4. For the invariant compact-quotient family of w7-1/n1, take H=∫X h0^n, μ=h0^n/H, V_W={θA:A∈W}, and identify its unit-volume hypersurface with S_W. Its unique Dμ=1 minimizing Gauduchon metric at A∈S_W is γA=θA. For all A,B∈S_W, the pointwise tensor inequalities on X are
   e^(−√n d_W(A,B))γA ≤ γB ≤ e^(√n d_W(A,B))γA.
   Finite total path length forces these normalized minimizing metrics to remain uniformly positive and uniformly bounded. Every intrinsic Cauchy sequence of the normalized minimizing metrics converges in C∞ to the smooth positive invariant minimizer γA of its coefficient limit A∈S_W. Every point of the completion has the canonical smooth positive current representative θA, and no additional Cauchy-boundary current is added. Other potential representatives of a fixed background do not constitute additional points of this specified cone or its completion.

5. In that geometric family, the positive-current-representable coefficient cone and the coefficient closure of C_W are exactly W∩{A≥0}, with canonical smooth semipositive representatives θA; the zero background has only the zero positive-current representative. Suppose Aj∈C_W converges in coefficients to a nonzero singular A0≥0. Then λ(Aj)→0, the normalized matrices Âj=Aj/λ(Aj) belong to S_W, λmax(Âj)→∞, and for every fixed A*∈S_W and all sufficiently large j,
   d_W(A*,Âj) ≥ (1/√n)log[λmax(Aj)/(λ(Aj)λmax(A*))]
   = |log det Aj|/(n√n)+O(1) →∞,
   where O(1) remains bounded along the sequence. Thus no nonzero semipositive singular coefficient-boundary current becomes a finite-distance unit-volume completion point after normalization.

   A sequence approaching the zero coefficient matrix need not have degenerating normalized matrices: if Aj=tjA* with tj>0 and tj→0, then Âj=A*. Such radial collapse adds no unit-volume point, and zero is not a point of the unit-volume completion.

6. For every piecewise C¹ path A(t) in C_W,
   |d(log λ(A(t)))/dt|=|(1/n)tr(A(t)⁻¹A′(t))|≤√gA(t)(A′(t),A′(t)).
   Hence d_C_W(A,B)≥|log λ(A)−log λ(B)|. In the unnormalized cone, every determinant-zero coefficient boundary is infinitely distant, and λ^n tending to zero or infinity forces distance from any fixed point to tend to infinity.

The full-matrix distance is only a lower bound for a proper W; its attaining full-matrix curve is not asserted to lie in W. The completeness and all upper estimates above concern the fixed specified cone, not an enlarged cone. The current and Gauduchon assertions use the hypotheses of w7-1/n1 and do not classify arbitrary nonclosed cones or arbitrary probability volumes.
reconstruction.proof:
We first prove the matrix metric facts directly; no external metric-distance, geodesic-completeness, or properness theorem is imported. Write ‖·‖F for the Frobenius norm and ≤ for Hermitian matrix order.

1. Distance on the full positive cone. Congruence by an invertible P is an isometry. Indeed, (PAP*)^(−1)=P^(−*)A^(−1)P^(−1), and substitution of PAP*, PUP*, PZP* into the metric reduces its trace to tr(A^(−1)UA^(−1)Z) by cyclicity.

Here is the required global lower bound. For a positive matrix M, spectral calculus and the scalar integral formula for logarithm give
log M=∫0∞[(1/(1+s))I−(M+sI)^(−1)] ds,
D log_M[U]=∫0∞(M+sI)^(−1)U(M+sI)^(−1) ds.
The derivative formula follows by differentiating the inverse under the integral; on a neighborhood with eigenvalues bounded away from zero the derivative integrand has an integrable bound. In a unitary basis diagonalizing M with eigenvalues di>0, this derivative has entries cijUij, where
cii=1/di,   cij=(log di−log dj)/(di−dj) if di≠dj,
and the continuous value 1/di is used when di=dj. The elementary inequality
√(di dj)|cij|≤1
follows, for di≠dj, by putting di/dj=e^(2s): the left side is |s/sinh s|≤1. The diagonal case is equality. Consequently
‖D log_M[U]‖F²≤Σi,j |Uij|²/(di dj)=‖M^(−1/2)UM^(−1/2)‖F².

For any piecewise C¹ path from I to B, integrate this differential inequality and then the Euclidean triangle inequality for log M(t). Its length is at least ‖log B‖F/√n. Congruence by A^(−1/2) gives, for any path from A to B,
length ≥ (1/√n)‖log(A^(−1/2)BA^(−1/2))‖F.
Conversely set C=A^(−1/2)BA^(−1/2), L=log C, and M(t)=A^(1/2)e^(tL)A^(1/2). In the congruent coordinates e^(tL), the matrix and its derivative commute, and the speed is constantly ‖L‖F/√n. Thus this curve attains the lower bound and proves the full-cone distance formula.

Its determinant is det A·(det C)^t. If det A=det B, then det C=1 and the curve stays in that constant-determinant hypersurface. The full-cone lower bound and this admissible curve prove the same intrinsic formula there. This establishes assertion 1 without an imported metric-geometry result.

2. Estimates in the fixed W. The set C_W is a nonempty open convex cone in W. Homogeneity gives λ(tA)=tλ(A), and Dλ_A[A]=λ(A)>0, so S_W is a smooth hypersurface (a singleton is allowed when dim W=1). The full-cone distance is a lower bound on its intrinsic distance because every path in S_W is also a full-cone path.

For the upper bound let A,B∈S_W, U=B−A, C(t)=A+tU, and N(t)=C(t)/λ(C(t)). The entire segment C is in C_W. Since W is linear and λ is positively homogeneous, N is a path in the specified S_W, with endpoints A and B. Put
K=C^(−1/2)UC^(−1/2),   a=(log λ(C))′=(1/n)tr K.
Then N′=(U−aC)/λ(C). Substitution into the metric and cyclicity of trace give precisely
g_N(N′,N′)=(1/n)tr(K−aI)²=(1/n)tr K²−(1/n²)(tr K)².
With m=min{λmin(A),λmin(B)}, we have C(t)≥mI, whence
‖K‖F≤‖C^(−1/2)‖op²‖U‖F≤‖U‖F/m.
Thus the speed is at most ‖A−B‖F/(√n m), and integration proves the stated upper bound. It also proves path connectedness using only paths in W.

Let d=d_W(A,B). The lower bound implies ‖log(A^(−1/2)BA^(−1/2))‖F≤√n d, so every eigenvalue of this logarithm lies in [−√n d,√n d]. Exponentiation and congruence give
e^(−√n d)A≤B≤e^(√n d)A.
For completeness, the same estimates can also be obtained directly for any finite-length path A(t). For a fixed nonzero v,
|d log(v*A(t)v)/dt|≤‖A(t)^(−1/2)A′(t)A(t)^(−1/2)‖op≤√n·speed(t).
Integration for every v yields the order bounds with that path's length. This proves all estimates in assertion 2, including their pathwise version.

3. Topology, completeness, and properness. Coefficient convergence B_j→A∈S_W implies intrinsic convergence by the upper bound, since the smallest eigenvalues are eventually bounded below by a positive constant. Conversely d_W(A,B_j)→0 implies coefficient convergence by the order bounds: if δ_j=√n d_W(A,B_j), then
‖B_j−A‖op≤(e^(δ_j)−1)‖A‖op→0.
Thus the two topologies agree.

Fix A*∈S_W and R<∞. Its intrinsic closed R-ball is contained in the coefficient-compact set
K_R={A∈W: H det A=1, e^(−√n R)A*≤A≤e^(√n R)A*}.
This set is closed and bounded in the finite-dimensional space W, and its lower order bound ensures positive definiteness throughout. A coefficient limit of points in the ball is in K_R and, by the already proved upper estimate, is their intrinsic limit. Continuity of distance then keeps it in the ball. The ball is therefore coefficient-closed in K_R and compact; topology agreement makes it intrinsically compact. This proves properness directly.

Every intrinsic Cauchy sequence is bounded. It has a coefficient-convergent subsequence in one such compact set, with limit A∈S_W. The upper bound makes the subsequence converge intrinsically, and the Cauchy property makes the whole sequence converge to A. Hence S_W is complete and its completion adds nothing. Conversely any coefficient-convergent sequence with limit in S_W is intrinsically convergent and therefore Cauchy. This proves the exact Cauchy criterion.

The same order bounds show that bounded distances from A* imply uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds on the eigenvalues of A*^(−1/2)AA*^(−1/2). Conversely such eigenvalue bounds imply uniform bounds on coefficients and a uniform positive lower bound on λmin(A). The fixed-W upper estimate to A* then bounds the intrinsic distances.

In particular the order inequalities give
λmax(A)≤e^(√n d_W(A*,A))λmax(A*),
λmin(A)≥e^(−√n d_W(A*,A))λmin(A*).
Thus λmax(A_j)→∞ or λmin(A_j)→0 forces d_W(A*,A_j)→∞. More generally, a sequence eventually outside every coefficient-compact subset must eventually leave each closed intrinsic ball, since those balls are coefficient compact. Its distances therefore tend to infinity. There are no Cauchy boundary points at finite singular matrices, at unbounded coefficients, or elsewhere at infinity.

4. Interpretation through minimizing Gauduchon metrics. Apply w7-1/n1 with its compact quotient, its coframe, its H, and its invariant probability volume. Its hypotheses give λμ(θA)=λ(A), and its unique Dμ=1 minimizer is θA/λ(A). On S_W it is γA=θA. Matrix order is equivalent to pointwise order of these invariant Hermitian forms; consequently
e^(−√n d_W(A,B))γA≤γB≤e^(√n d_W(A,B))γA
at every point of X. The pathwise version proves uniform upper and positive lower tensor bounds along any path of finite total length. Moreover its tails have lengths tending to zero, so an endpoint approached along a finite-total-length path is Cauchy and hence converges to a positive matrix in S_W.

For any intrinsic Cauchy sequence the coefficient convergence proved above yields convergence of θAj in C∞: the coefficients converge in a fixed finite-dimensional span of smooth forms. The limit is the positive invariant metric γA=θA and is again the unique normalized minimizer by w7-1/n1. Every completion point therefore has this canonical smooth positive current representative, with no additional Cauchy-boundary current. A different current or potential representing the same background does not define a different coefficient point.

5. Coefficient-boundary currents and normalization. By w7-1/n1, positive-current representability in W is exactly A≥0, the coefficient closure of C_W, with canonical representative θA. That result also proves that the zero background has only the zero positive-current representative.

Suppose A_j∈C_W converges to a nonzero singular A0≥0. Then det A_j→0, λ(A_j)→0, and λmax(A_j)→λmax(A0)>0. The normalized matrices Â_j=A_j/λ(A_j) lie in S_W and have λmax(Â_j)→∞. The preceding order bound, applied to A* and Â_j, implies
 d_W(A*,Â_j) ≥ (1/√n)log(λmax(Â_j)/λmax(A*))
 = (1/√n)log[λmax(A_j)/(λ(A_j)λmax(A*))].
For all sufficiently large j the last expression equals
|log det A_j|/(n√n) + [log λmax(A_j)−(log H)/n−log λmax(A*)]/√n.
The bracket is bounded, so this is the asserted lower bound with O(1), and tends to infinity. Thus no nonzero singular semipositive coefficient-boundary current becomes a finite-distance unit-volume point after normalization.

A zero coefficient limit requires a separate statement. For A_j=t_jA*, t_j↓0, homogeneity gives λ(A_j)=t_j and Â_j=A*. Thus radial collapse may normalize to an already existing point. It adds no new point, and the zero current itself is not a point of the unit-volume completion. Arbitrary approaches to zero are governed by the positive-definite convergence criterion for their normalized matrices, not by the zero coefficient limit alone.

6. Unnormalized distance and volume. For a piecewise C¹ path A(t)∈C_W put K=A^(−1/2)A′A^(−1/2). The determinant derivative and Cauchy–Schwarz on the real eigenvalues of K give
|(log λ(A))′|=|tr K|/n≤(tr K²/n)^(1/2)=√g_A(A′,A′).
Integrating and taking the infimum over paths proves
d_C_W(A,B)≥|log λ(A)−log λ(B)|.
Any coefficient limit on the determinant-zero boundary has λ→0, so its distance from a fixed interior point tends to infinity. The same lower bound applies when λ^n tends to zero or infinity, proving assertion 6.

The only use of the full positive cone was the directly proved lower bound. The upper paths, Cauchy convergence, and properness arguments all stay inside the fixed W. In particular, a full-matrix attaining curve is not asserted to belong to a proper W. The current and minimizing-metric conclusions use exactly the geometric hypotheses and invariant μ of w7-1/n1, not an arbitrary nonclosed cone.

notes.text:
COMPLETE SOLUTION FOR A SPECIFIED GENUINELY NONCLOSED FAMILY.
The task admits the following sufficient-condition completion theorem, with a concrete non-Kähler, genuinely nonclosed family. The theorem deliberately does not claim a classification of arbitrary finite-dimensional nonclosed cones.

I. EXPLICIT GEOMETRY AND THE SPECIFIED CONE.
Let G be C³ with multiplication
  (z1,z2,z3)·(w1,w2,w3)=(z1+w1,z2+w2,z3+w3+z1w2),
and let Γ consist of triples in Z[i]³. This is a subgroup: the group law and inverse preserve Gaussian integer coordinates. Γ is discrete. Its left action is free and properly discontinuous: for a compact K⊂G, any γ with γK∩K≠∅ belongs to the compact KK⁻¹, which contains only finitely many Γ-elements.
The quotient X=Γ\G is compact. In fact, every coset has a representative with the real and imaginary parts of all three coordinates in [0,1]. To see this, choose γ1,γ2∈Z[i] to reduce z1,z2 modulo the lattice, then choose γ3 to reduce z3+γ1z2. Away from the boundary the representative is unique: two representatives in the half-open unit cube first force γ1=γ2=0 and then γ3=0. Thus a unit real six-cube is a measurable fundamental domain. X is a connected compact complex manifold of dimension three.
The left-invariant holomorphic forms
  α1=dz1,  α2=dz2,  α3=dz3−z1dz2
are Γ-invariant and descend to a global coframe on X. They satisfy
  dα1=dα2=0,  dα3=−α1∧α2.
For every Hermitian 3×3 matrix A put
  θA=(i/(2π))Σj,k Ajk αj∧barαk.
Take the fully specified real nine-dimensional space V={θA:A∈Herm(3)}. Set h0=θI and choose μ=h0³/H, H=∫Xh0³. The auxiliary smooth positive form h in the question may be h0; nothing in λ depends on that auxiliary choice. Since α1∧α2∧α3=dz1∧dz2∧dz3, the volume density h0³ in the coordinate fundamental domain is (6/π³) times ordinary real Lebesgue volume. Hence
  H=6/π³.
This also explicitly specifies μ.
Applying the proved averaging argument in n1, V has no nonzero smooth dd^c direction, and the question's positive-representative cone is precisely
  C={θA:A>0}.
This is not merely a positive cone inserted into a larger space of representatives: smooth dd^c changes cannot enlarge it. Moreover every element of C is nonclosed. Directly, the coefficient of α1∧α2∧barα3 in ∂θA is −(i/(2π))A33, and A33>0. Thus dθA≠0. As d(dd^c u)=0, none of these backgrounds has a d-closed representative in its dd^c class.

II. EXACT VOLUME, HESSIAN, AND MINIMIZING METRICS.
All needed analytic arguments are proved in n1 rather than imported. In particular every θA with A>0 is balanced; it is an admissible Gauduchon competitor. Its top form is (H det A)μ. Pointwise arithmetic-geometric mean against arbitrary Gauduchon competitors proves exactly
  Vμ(θA)=(6/π³)det A,
  λμ(θA)=((6/π³)det A)^(1/3).
There is no appeal to a formal Hessian or a Monge–Ampère existence assertion. Actual differentiation of this established determinant formula gives
  gA(U,Z)=(1/3)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z).
This is a smooth positive definite metric on V's positive cone.
The unique minimizing Gauduchon metric after fixing Dμ(γ)=1 is
  γA=θA/((6/π³)det A)^(1/3).
Indeed equality in arithmetic-geometric mean requires a conformal multiple of θA, and its Gauduchon condition plus balancedness forces that multiple to be constant by the energy argument of n1. This supplies explicit minimizing metrics at every point, not just minimizing sequences.
The unit-volume hypersurface is
  S={θA:A>0, det A=π³/6}.
On S, γA=θA.

III. COMPLETE INTRINSIC COMPLETION AND ALL CAUCHY POINTS.
The self-contained spectral length proof in n2 yields the exact intrinsic distance on this specified full cone's unit-volume slice:
  dS(θA,θB)=(1/√3)||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||F.
The attaining curve is θM(t), with
  M(t)=A¹/²(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)^tA¹/².
It has determinant π³/6 throughout and lies inside the specified V and S. Thus the displayed formula is not an extrinsic shortcut through an enlarged cone.
Every intrinsic Cauchy sequence has coefficient matrices converging to a positive-definite A with det A=π³/6, and conversely every such coefficient convergence is intrinsic convergence. This is proved by the quantitative lower and normalized-chord upper bounds in n2. Consequently
  the metric completion of S is S itself;
  there are no Cauchy boundary points, at finite coefficients or at infinity.
In fact closed bounded intrinsic balls are compact. All completion points have the canonical smooth positive current representative θA, which is also their unique Dμ=1 minimizing Gauduchon metric. Thus this is a complete classification of the completion, not just a list of some excluded coefficient-boundary points.
For a scalar reference A*=aI, a=(π³/6)^(1/3), the distance is particularly explicit:
  dS(θA*,θA)²=(1/3)Σi=1³ (log(λi(A)/a))².
The sum of these three logarithms is zero on S. Hence any eigenvalue tending to zero or infinity forces infinite distance. There are no additional asymptotic Cauchy directions.

IV. CURRENT REPRESENTATIVES AND FINITE/INFINITE DISTANCE ESTIMATES.
Positive-current representability of a coefficient background θA, even permitting distributional potentials, is precisely A≥0, by the distributional averaging proof of n1. Its canonical representative is the smooth semipositive current θA. The zero background has only the zero positive-current representative. Thus the entire positive-current coefficient closure is identified explicitly. It must not be confused with the metric completion.
On S, the unique normalized minimizing metrics obey at every point of X
  e^(−√3 dS(A,B))γA ≤ γB ≤ e^(√3 dS(A,B))γA.
Therefore finite length gives uniform lower and upper positivity bounds on these minimizing metrics. A Cauchy sequence of them converges smoothly to a positive invariant metric. Conversely every minimizing-metric eigenvalue collapse or explosion on S occurs at infinite distance, quantitatively detected by the logarithmic distance above.
More concretely, suppose Aj>0 converges to a nonzero singular semipositive A0. The unnormalized coefficient boundary has the current θA0, but λμ(θAj)→0. Its unit-volume normalized minimizing metrics correspond to
  Âj=Aj/λμ(θAj),
and their largest eigenvalue tends to infinity. The rigorous estimate from n2 is
  dS(A*,Âj) ≥ |log det Aj|/(3√3)+O(1) →∞.
All nonzero semipositive coefficient boundary currents are therefore excluded from the completion even after attempting unit-volume normalization. Approaching the zero coefficient matrix can be pure radial scaling; its normalization may converge to an existing point of S, but it never gives a zero-current point of the completion. On the unnormalized cone, distance dominates the change in log λ, so volume tending to zero or infinity has infinite length as well.
This distinguishes finite from infinite distance directly in terms of the actual minimizing Gauduchon metrics: finite Cauchy behavior is exactly smooth convergence to a uniformly positive invariant minimizer; every true unit-volume degeneracy is infinitely distant.

V. A MORE GENERAL SUFFICIENT-CONDITION CLASSIFICATION, WITH THE CONE KEPT FIXED.
The same conclusions hold on every compact quotient Γ\G in n1, with the normalized invariant μ, and every separately specified real linear subspace W⊂Herm(n) containing a positive matrix. Its prescribed space is V_W={θA:A∈W}; its prescribed cone is exactly W∩{A>0}; its volume is H det A; and its unit-volume completion adds no points.
For proper W the full-matrix formula is only an intrinsic lower bound, not necessarily an equality. Intrinsic upper estimates instead use the normalized straight chord entirely inside W:
  d_{S_W}(A,B) ≤ ||A−B||F/(√n min{λmin A,λmin B}).
Together with the full-matrix lower estimate, this proves the complete Cauchy classification and properness without ever enlarging the specified cone in an upper-bound argument. On nonabelian G all its positive invariant backgrounds are genuinely nonclosed.
The full Iwasawa cone above is the fully explicit instance, with real cone dimension nine and unit-volume dimension eight. It is different from a closed projective product cone or a blowup-surface cone, and provides the requested nonclosed family. The conclusion in this family is that no positive-current coefficient boundary is a finite-distance unit-volume boundary; it does not assert the same for general cones, where finite-distance boundary behavior may occur.
No external metric-geometry theorem or source premise is required: the distance formula, properness, and completeness were independently proved in n2 by spectral variation, matrix inequalities, and curves inside the fixed cone.

reconstruction.statement:
Let G=C³ with the complex Lie-group law
   (z1,z2,z3)·(w1,w2,w3)=(z1+w1,z2+w2,z3+w3+z1w2),
and let Γ consist of triples in Z[i]³. Then Γ is a discrete subgroup, its left action on G is free and properly discontinuous, and X=Γ\G is a connected compact complex manifold of complex dimension three. Every coset has a representative whose six real coordinate components belong to [0,1]; the corresponding half-open unit real six-cube is a measurable fundamental domain.

The forms α1=dz1, α2=dz2, and α3=dz3−z1dz2 descend to a global left-invariant holomorphic coframe on X and satisfy dα1=dα2=0 and dα3=−α1∧α2. For A∈Herm(3), define θA=(i/(2π))Σj,k Ajk αj∧barαk. Specify V={θA:A∈Herm(3)}, h=h0=θI, H=∫X h0³, and μ=h0³/H. On the coordinate fundamental domain, h0³ is (6/π³) times ordinary real Lebesgue volume, so H=6/π³ and μ is a smooth positive probability volume. Use dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂ and the definitions of Dμ, λμ, Vμ, and g=−D²log λμ in w7-1/n1.

1. The specified real space V has dimension nine and satisfies V∩dd^c C∞(X,R)={0}. Its backgrounds admitting a smooth positive representative are exactly C={θA:A>0}. Every θA∈C is balanced and Gauduchon, but is genuinely nonclosed; no addition of dd^c u gives it a d-closed representative.

2. For every A>0,
   Vμ(θA)=(6/π³)det A,
   λμ(θA)=((6/π³)det A)^(1/3),
   gA(U,Z)=(1/3)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z),   U,Z∈Herm(3).
   The Hessian metric is smooth and positive definite. The unique Gauduchon metric attaining the defining infimum and satisfying Dμ(γ)=1 is
   γA=θA/((6/π³)det A)^(1/3).
   The unit-volume hypersurface is the real eight-dimensional manifold
   S={θA:A>0, det A=π³/6},
   and its normalized minimizing metric is γA=θA.

3. The intrinsic path distance on this specified S is exactly
   dS(θA,θB)=(1/√3)||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||F.
   It is attained by θM(t), where M(t)=A¹/²(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)^tA¹/², 0≤t≤1. This curve lies in the specified V and has determinant π³/6 throughout.

   A sequence (θAj)⊂S is intrinsic Cauchy if and only if Aj converges in coefficients to a positive-definite matrix A with det A=π³/6. Consequently S is complete and proper, its metric completion is S itself, and there are no Cauchy boundary points at finite coefficients or at infinity. Every completion point has the canonical smooth positive current representative θA, which is also its unique Dμ=1 minimizing Gauduchon metric.

   If a=(π³/6)^(1/3) and A*=aI, then
   dS(θA*,θA)²=(1/3)Σi=1³(log(λi(A)/a))²,
   Σi=1³ log(λi(A)/a)=0.
   Any eigenvalue tending to zero or infinity on S therefore forces distance from θA* to tend to infinity.

4. For every A∈Herm(3), θA has a positive-current representative θA+dd^c u with u a real distribution if and only if A≥0. Every such A has the canonical smooth semipositive representative θA. The zero background has only the zero positive-current representative. Thus the positive-current-representable coefficient cone is exactly the coefficient closure {θA:A≥0}; it is not the metric completion of S.

   For all A,B∈S and every x∈X,
   e^(−√3 dS(θA,θB))γA ≤ γB ≤ e^(√3 dS(θA,θB))γA.
   Finite total path length forces uniform upper and lower positivity bounds on these minimizing metrics. An intrinsic Cauchy sequence of them converges smoothly to a positive invariant minimizing metric. Every eigenvalue collapse or explosion of the normalized minimizing metrics on S is infinitely distant.

   Suppose Aj>0 converges to a nonzero singular semipositive A0. Then θA0 is a coefficient-boundary positive-current representative, λμ(θAj)→0, and the unit-volume normalized minimizing matrices
   Âj=Aj/λμ(θAj)
   have λmax(Âj)→∞. For every fixed A*∈S,
   dS(θA*,θÂj) ≥ |log det Aj|/(3√3)+O(1) →∞,
   with a bounded O(1) term. Hence every nonzero semipositive singular coefficient-boundary current is excluded from the unit-volume completion even after normalization. Approaching the zero coefficient matrix may be pure radial scaling and may normalize to an existing point of S, but never adds a zero-current completion point. On the unnormalized cone, intrinsic distance dominates |log λμ(θA)−log λμ(θB)|, so volume tending to zero or infinity has infinite distance from every fixed interior point.

5. More generally, let n≥2, let G be any connected complex Lie group with a discrete left-translation subgroup Γ such that Γ\G is compact, fix a descended left-invariant holomorphic coframe, and define θA, h0, H=∫X h0^n, and μ=h0^n/H as in w7-1/n1. For every separately specified real linear subspace W⊂Herm(n) containing a positive-definite matrix, let V_W={θA:A∈W}. Then V_W has no nonzero smooth dd^c direction, its prescribed positive-representative cone is exactly {θA:A∈W,A>0}, its variational volume is H det A, its Hessian metric is (1/n)tr(A⁻¹UA⁻¹Z), and its unique Dμ=1 minimizing metric is θA/(H det A)^(1/n). Positive-current representability in V_W is exactly A≥0.

   Its unit-volume hypersurface S_W={A∈W:A>0,H det A=1} is complete and proper, with no additional Cauchy boundary points. Its intrinsic Cauchy sequences are exactly those converging in coefficients to a positive-definite matrix in S_W. For all A,B∈S_W,
   (1/√n)||log(A⁻¹/²BA⁻¹/²)||F ≤ dS_W(A,B)
   ≤ ||A−B||F/(√n min{λmin(A),λmin(B)}).
   The upper estimate concerns paths lying in this fixed W. For a proper W, equality with the full-matrix distance is not asserted. The minimizing-metric comparisons, exclusion of nonzero singular coefficient-boundary currents after normalization, and radial-zero distinction of w7-1/n2 hold for each such fixed cone. If the Lie algebra of G is nonabelian, all its positive invariant backgrounds are genuinely nonclosed.

This is a completion theorem for the specified invariant family with its normalized invariant μ, including the explicit nonclosed nine-dimensional Iwasawa cone above; it is not a classification of arbitrary finite-dimensional nonclosed cones or arbitrary μ.
reconstruction.proof:
We first construct and verify the explicit quotient, then apply the two supporting results with their hypotheses checked.

Construction of X and its invariant volume. The displayed multiplication is associative: the third coordinates of (z·w)·v and z·(w·v) are both z3+w3+v3+z1w2+z1v2+w1v2. The identity is 0, and the inverse of z is (−z1,−z2,−z3+z1z2). All operations are holomorphic, so G is a connected complex Lie group of dimension three.

The Gaussian-integer triples are closed under multiplication and inversion and form a closed discrete subgroup Γ. Left translations act freely by cancellation. They act properly discontinuously: for compact K,L⊂G, an element with γK∩L≠∅ lies in the compact set LK^(−1), which contains only finitely many elements of Γ. Freeness and this property give quotient charts on sufficiently small open sets with disjoint translates; the transition maps are holomorphic left translations. Thus Γ\G is a complex manifold of dimension three, and it is connected because G is connected.

Let Q=[0,1)+i[0,1) and F=Q³. For any z choose a,b∈Z[i] such that z1+a,z2+b∈Q. Then choose c∈Z[i] such that z3+a z2+c∈Q. The left translate by (a,b,c) lies in F. If two elements of F differ by a left translate (a,b,c), their first-coordinate difference forces a=0, their second-coordinate difference forces b=0, and their third-coordinate difference then forces c=0. Thus F is a measurable fundamental domain. Its closed unit six-cube is compact and maps onto X, proving compactness and also the asserted closed-cube representative property.

Under left translation by z, the first two forms dz1,dz2 are invariant and
L_z*(dz3−z1 dz2)=dw3+z1dw2−(z1+w1)dw2=dw3−w1dw2.
Thus α1,α2,α3 descend to a global holomorphic coframe. They obey dα1=dα2=0 and dα3=−α1∧α2. Their dual fields on G are
Z1=∂/∂z1,   Z2=∂/∂z2+z1∂/∂z3,   Z3=∂/∂z3,
so [Z1,Z2]=Z3 and the Lie algebra is nonabelian.

The triangular coframe change has determinant one. In the top wedge, the terms involving −z1dz2 in α3 vanish against the preceding factors. Since (i/(2π))dz∧dbar z=(1/π)dx∧dy, direct expansion gives
h0³=3! Πj=1³[(i/(2π))αj∧bar αj]=(6/π³) dx1∧dy1∧dx2∧dy2∧dx3∧dy3.
The domain F has real Euclidean volume one and its boundary has zero volume. Integrating the descended form over this fundamental domain therefore gives H=6/π³. The form μ=h0³/H is a smooth positive probability volume, as required.

1–2. Cone, variational volume, Hessian, and minimizers. Apply w7-1/n1 with n=3, this connected compact quotient, its descended left-invariant holomorphic coframe, W=Herm(3), and the just computed H and μ. All its hypotheses have been verified. The coframe identifies Herm(3) injectively with V, whose real dimension is 3²=9. That result proves
V∩dd^c C∞(X,R)={0},   C={θA:A>0},
and every positive θA is balanced and Gauduchon. Nonabelianity, verified by [Z1,Z2]=Z3, invokes precisely its nonclosedness conclusion: none of these θA is closed and no addition of dd^c u makes it closed.

Its variational calculation gives the exact formulas
Vμ(θA)=(6/π³)det A,
λμ(θA)=((6/π³)det A)^(1/3),
g_A(U,Z)=(1/3)tr(A^(−1)UA^(−1)Z).
The metric is smooth positive definite by that same result. Its unique minimizing Gauduchon metric with Dμ=1 is
γA=θA/((6/π³)det A)^(1/3).
Consequently S is exactly {θA:A>0,det A=π³/6}, and its normalized minimizer is θA. It is a smooth real eight-dimensional hypersurface: the determinant derivative in the radial direction A is 3 det A≠0, in the nine-dimensional open cone.

3. Exact intrinsic distance and completion. Apply w7-1/n2 with n=3, W=Herm(3), and H=6/π³. Its metric is exactly the Hessian metric just established. Here the specified space is the full matrix space, so its full constant-determinant distance formula applies intrinsically to this very S:
dS(θA,θB)=(1/√3)‖log(A^(−1/2)BA^(−1/2))‖F.
The attaining matrix curve is M(t)=A^(1/2)(A^(−1/2)BA^(−1/2))^tA^(1/2). It lies in this specified V. Since det A=det B=π³/6, its determinant is that same number throughout, so it lies in S, not merely in an enlarged space.

The completeness, properness, and exact Cauchy criterion of w7-1/n2 show that a sequence in S is Cauchy exactly when its matrices converge to a positive-definite matrix with determinant π³/6. There are no additional completion points. Each existing point has its canonical smooth positive representative θA, which is its unique Dμ=1 minimizing metric.

For a=(π³/6)^(1/3), the basepoint A*=aI belongs to S. The eigenvalues of A*^(−1/2)AA*^(−1/2) are λi(A)/a, and hence
 dS(θA*,θA)²=(1/3)Σi=1³(log(λi(A)/a))².
Their logarithms sum to log(det A/a³)=0. Any eigenvalue tending to zero or infinity forces this distance to tend to infinity. This explicitly rules out both finite singular coefficient limits and eigenvalue escape at infinity as Cauchy boundary points.

4. Currents and the estimates on minimizing metrics. The distributional assertion of w7-1/n1, with these same verified hypotheses, gives
θA+dd^c u≥0 for some real distribution u ⇔ A≥0.
For A≥0 the canonical representative is θA itself, and the zero background has only the zero positive-current representative. Thus the positive-current-representable coefficient cone is exactly {θA:A≥0}; this coefficient closure is not the metric completion of S.

On S the normalized minimizer is γA=θA. The minimizing-metric comparison of w7-1/n2 becomes, at every x∈X,
e^(−√3 dS(θA,θB))γA≤γB≤e^(√3 dS(θA,θB))γA.
Its pathwise version bounds the minimizing metrics uniformly above and uniformly positively below along any path of finite total length. Its Cauchy criterion gives smooth convergence of any intrinsic Cauchy sequence of these invariant metrics to a positive invariant minimizing metric. Eigenvalue collapse or explosion of the normalized metrics forces infinite distance by the bounds, equivalently by the explicit basepoint formula.

If A_j→A0≥0 with A0 nonzero and singular, then det A_j→0, λμ(θAj)→0, and the normalized minimizing matrices Â_j=A_j/λμ(θAj) belong to S. Their largest eigenvalues tend to infinity because λmax(A_j) tends to the positive number λmax(A0). For any fixed A*∈S, the lower estimate of w7-1/n2 gives
 dS(θA*,θÂj)≥(1/√3)log[λmax(A_j)/(λμ(θAj)λmax(A*))]
 = |log det A_j|/(3√3)+O(1)→∞.
The remainder is bounded: it is [log λmax(A_j)−(log(6/π³))/3−log λmax(A*)]/√3. Thus these semipositive coefficient-boundary currents are not finite-distance unit-volume points, even after normalization.

For comparison, A_j=t_jA* with t_j↓0 tends to the zero coefficient matrix but normalizes to A*. This adds no unit-volume point and never makes the zero current a completion point. Finally w7-1/n2 proves, on the specified unnormalized cone, that intrinsic distance dominates the absolute difference of log λμ. Thus volume tending to zero or infinity forces infinite distance there, including pure radial collapse.

5. General specified invariant family. Let G, Γ, the descended coframe, n≥2, and the separately fixed W satisfy exactly the hypotheses in the last assertion. The quotient is connected because G is connected; it is compact by hypothesis. The coframe makes h0 positive, H=∫Xh0^n finite and positive, and μ=h0^n/H a smooth positive probability volume. W contains a positive-definite matrix by hypothesis. These are all hypotheses of w7-1/n1, so it gives injectivity of A↦θA, no nonzero smooth dd^c direction, the positive-representative cone W∩{A>0}, the exact volume H det A, the trace Hessian metric, the unique normalized minimizing metric θA/(H det A)^(1/n), and positive-current representability exactly when A≥0. If the Lie algebra is nonabelian it also gives genuine nonclosedness of every positive background.

Now w7-1/n2 applies with this n,W,H, because the preceding variational and Hessian formulas identify its matrix hypersurface and metric with this fixed geometric S_W. It proves completeness and properness, no new Cauchy boundary points, and the positive-definite coefficient-limit criterion. Its estimates are precisely
(1/√n)‖log(A^(−1/2)BA^(−1/2))‖F≤dS_W(A,B)
≤‖A−B‖F/(√n min{λmin(A),λmin(B)}).
The upper estimate uses the normalized segment in this very W. A proper W need not contain the full-matrix attaining curve, and no equality with the full-matrix distance is claimed. The same result supplies the minimizing-metric bounds, the divergent normalization estimate at every nonzero singular semipositive coefficient limit, and the separate treatment of a zero radial limit.

This proves a full intrinsic completion theorem for each of the specified invariant cones, including the explicit nine-dimensional genuinely nonclosed Iwasawa cone constructed above. It does not classify arbitrary finite-dimensional nonclosed cones, nor change the invariant probability volume or enlarge a specified cone when measuring its distance. All metric-distance and properness statements used here were proved directly in w7-1/n2 rather than imported from an external metric-geometry source.
